content:
An heir sought the division of specific Italian and Swiss assets but later attempted to include Venezuelan properties and claims of "fictitious" ownership during the trial. This case hinged on the distinction between the initial claim (citazione) and new claims (mutatio libelli) under Article 183 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as well as the right of habitation (Art. 540 CC). The interpretive challenge was whether a division could be expanded to new assets after the initial pleadings. The court ruled that adding assets or challenging the validity of past transactions constitutes an inadmissible "new claim" because it introduces entirely new inquiry themes. Regarding the right of habitation, the judge applied the principle that this right applies only to the actual family residence; if the couple habitually lived abroad, a secondary house in Italy does not qualify as the family home, and no value deduction for such a right can be applied.
